name: Sitagliptin and metformin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: One tablet (sitagliptin 50 mg with metformin 500 mg, 850 mg or 1 g) twice daily with meals; maximum sitagliptin 100 mg and metformin 2,000 mg per day

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Drugs that reduce metformin clearance (ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine)

key_interactions.action: Consider lower insulin or sulfonylurea dose.

key_interactions.effect: Contrast-induced kidney injury can precipitate lactic acidosis (label).
key_interactions.action: Hold per label 2.3; recheck eGFR at 48 hours.

contraindications: Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis
Serious hypersensitivity to sitagliptin or metformin
monitoring: Hold for iodinated contrast per label

pk.half_life: Sitagliptin about 12 hours; metformin about 6 hours (plasma)
pk.metabolism: Sitagliptin: minimal (CYP3A4, minor CYP2C8); metformin: not metabolized
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Sitagliptin about 79% unchanged in urine; metformin about 90% unchanged in urine
pk.dialyzability: Metformin yes; sitagliptin modest (13.5% per session; label)
